title: ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE — Aruna v. State (not a real case)
facts: The appellant filed an appeal 95 days beyond the period of limitation.
The delay was attributed to the appellant's hospitalisation, supported by medical records.
The respondent opposed condonation, alleging the explanation was vague for part of the period.

issues.question: Whether sufficient cause was shown to condone the 95-day delay in filing the appeal?
issues.fact_trigger: Appeal filed 95 days late; delay explained by illness with medical records.

arguments.contention: Illness constituted sufficient cause; a liberal approach should be taken to advance substantial justice.
Each day's delay must be explained; the explanation for part of the period was vague.

holdings.issue: Whether sufficient cause was shown to condone the delay?
holdings.held: Delay condoned on terms of costs; medical records established sufficient cause and the liberal approach favours hearing the appeal on merits.
holdings.reasoning_summary: Substantial justice is preferred over a pedantic, day-to-day scrutiny where bona fide illness is shown.

relief_detail: Delay condoned subject to costs of Rs. 5,000; appeal restored to file.

treats_earlier_cases.note: Adopted the liberal-construction principle for S.5.
